# v0.2.1 annotation-scale gate

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

The release-scale fixture generates one million nonoverlapping BED3 records for one
sequence and runs the maintained streaming parser followed by a complete structured
clone of its publication graph. It is an explicit parser/publication gate, not a claim
about canvas rendering time or complete browser-process memory.

Run from the repository root with:

```sh
npm --prefix web run test:annotation-scale
```

Three 2026-08-29 reference-host runs produced the following median timings:

| Metric | Result | Gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Matching records | 1,000,000 | 1,000,000 maximum |
| Input bytes | 20,777,777 | 512 MiB maximum |
| Parse plus publication clone | 1,588 ms | 10,000 ms maximum |
| Publication clone | 1,038 ms | reported |
| Portable retained-data estimate | 176,000,000 bytes | 256 MiB maximum |

The roughly one-second complete publication clone confirms that the current nested
object representation can create a noticeable one-time publication pause at the
admission ceiling. Chunked/compact annotation publication remains scheduled for the
operational-scaling stage. The current file and matching-record limits prevent larger
single-file imports from expanding this representation without bound.
